{"claims":[{"claim_text":"The U.S. unilaterally withdrew from the nuclear agreement it signed with Iran in 2015, along with the UK, France, China, Russia and Germany.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Iran has remained compliant with the terms of the nuclear agreement.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Unless the U.S. sanctions are offset by the European signatories, Iran will increase its nuclear stockpile beyond the limit set in the agreement.",
"claim_types":["prediction"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The U.S. has claimed its aggression against Iran was predicated on preventing the country from developing nuclear weapons.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Both the U.S. and Israel have nuclear weapons.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"A 2007 National Intelligence Assessment concluded Iran halted its nuclear weapons program in 2003.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"The claim that Iran is developing nuclear weapons is an example of Washington’s willingness to manipulate facts to create a pretext for war, similar to the Gulf of Tonkin and Iraq’s alleged Weapons of Mass Destruction.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[2]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
```
